title: Midges Outbreak at Pandan Reservoir and Long-term Preventive Measures Planned
what_it_is: Midges Outbreak at Pandan Reservoir and Long-term Preventive Measures Planned

sections.label: Parliamentary questions on Pandan Reservoir midges
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister about midge outbreak causes, interventions, other water bodies, and long-term measures at Pandan Reservoir.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) what are the factors contributing to this year's midges outbreak at Pandan Reservoir; (b) how different is this outbreak compared to previous ones; (c) how experience from previous outbreaks has helped PUB to stay ahead of the curve in fighting the midges issue; and (d) why PUB has not been able to find a permanent solution to the occasional midges outbreaks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) what are the interventions used by PUB to counter the current midges outbreak at Pandan Reservoir; (b) how effective	have these measures been in controlling the midges population and mitigating its impact to the surrounding living environment; and (c) what additional new measures are being contemplated to help the community affected by the outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether there are other water bodies in Singapore experiencing a midges outbreak like that at Pandan Reservoir; and (b) whether PUB is able to predict, prevent and overcome such outbreaks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources regarding the persistent problems created by swarms of midges from Pandan Reservoir (a) what measures are being implemented to reduce the population of these chironomids; and (b) with rising temperatures, whether the Ministry will be considering long-term measures to prevent similar occurrences at this and possibly other reservoirs in the future.

sections.label: PUB midge larvae mitigation timeline
sections.summary: PUB saw more midge larvae from mid-June 2019 and acted swiftly when midges emerged in mid-July 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: At Pandan Reservoir, PUB observed an increase in midge larvae since mid-June 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: PUB kicked in mitigation measures swiftly when the midge emergence began in mid-July 2019.

sections.label: Rare dominant midge species
sections.summary: The current dominant midge species differs from the 2016 outbreak and is rare and not studied in detail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Unlike the midge emergence at Pandan Reservoir in 2016, the current dominant midge species is considered a rare one that has not been studied in great detail.

sections.label: Extended reservoir dyke netting
sections.summary: PUB added one kilometre of netting to the existing 0.5 kilometres on the reservoir dyke.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: PUB has also extended the existing 0.5 kilometres (km) of netting on the reservoir dyke by an additional one km.

sections.label: Residents describe severe midge outbreak
sections.summary: Midges stick to clothes, hair, eyes, nose and food, and this outbreak is the most severe and longest yet.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The midges stick to our clothes, really stick to your clothes, your hair, fly around your eyes, get into your nose, get into your food and they are everywhere.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This year's outbreak is the most severe we have witnessed yet and also persisted for the longest time, impacting the daily lives of our residents.

sections.label: Fogging pesticide certified safe
sections.summary: The fogging pesticide has undergone the WHO pesticide evaluation scheme and is certified safe and suitable for use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In fact, we are the ones who are intruding into their living spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This particular pesticide that we use in fogging has undergone the World Health Organization's (WHO's) pesticide evaluation scheme and has been certified safe and suitable for use.

sections.label: Safe biological larvicide in water
sections.summary: The larvicide put into the water is a safe biological larvicide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: On BTI, the larvicide that we use to put into the water, it is a safe biological larvicide.

sections.label: Lower Seletar Reservoir monitoring measures
sections.summary: Monitoring is done for every reservoir and appropriate measures are taken, with hope something can be done for Lower Seletar Reservoir.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I hope something can be done for the Lower Seletar Reservoir area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We do monitor for every reservoir and we take the appropriate measures.

sections.label: Midges protection for residents
sections.summary: PUB says midges may occur more regularly due to climate change, and help with screens or nets for residents will be studied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: In fact, PUB says that this may happen more regularly given the climate change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: We should really seriously consider helping residents with protection against the nuisance created by midges, whether helping, especially vulnerable families, with screens or HDB nets or definitely in public areas like bus stops, so that it is bearable for people to be in those places to take public transport.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: So, I urge the Minister to seriously consider this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We will study how we can help residents.

sections.label: More imminent dangers to Singapore
sections.summary: Other dangers are more imminent than midges and affect the whole of Singapore, and these issues will be studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: They present a more imminent danger than perhaps what midges will present to us, and not to just particular areas around the reservoirs but, in fact, to the whole of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: So, in consideration of all those issues, yes, we will study them.
